## 6 Analysis

### 6.1 What the direction is

Read through the J-lens itself, `+u_l` is not a concept:

- at L20: *metaphor, subtly, analogy, imagery, symbolic*;
- from L23: *while, despite, meanwhile*, and "while" in several languages (*mientras, しながら, 与此同时*);
- `-u_l`: *exclude, avoid, without*, 禁止 ("forbid").

Below layer 16 the readout of `u_l` is unrelated tokens in mixed scripts. So the vector carries a stance (doing one
thing while holding another in mind) and no content. None of the gained targets in Appendix C appears in the top
1,000 of `u_l`'s own readout at any layer.

### 6.2 The gain is computed, not read back

The cosine readout is linear in the state. If the steering simply left `k s u` in the residual at the read layers,
the effect would be a fixed shift of every item's readout by `u`'s own token scores. We test this directly. Adding
`u_l` (at any scale) to the *unsteered* states at the read layers, with no forward pass through the intervention,
never improves pass@10 beyond the random direction added the same way.

Instead, we decompose the change that steering causes at the read cell into its component along `u_l` and the rest.
The component along `u_l` carries essentially none of the gain. The rest carries 96% of it. Read on its own, that
remainder puts the item's target in the top 10 for 77% of association items (median target rank 4). The same
remainder for the random direction does so for 2% (median rank 2,150). Layer by layer, the remainder grows at layers
25-29 and peaks at 29. Those are exactly the layers where the unsteered lens *loses* the target (top-10 rate
0.10-0.14 at layers 26-28, against 0.25-0.31 at 20-24). Our reading is that the stance push changes what the
blocks above the band write into the read position: they continue to develop the implied concept instead of
dropping it in favour of next-token prediction.

### 6.3 Who gains

The gain grows with how deep the target was. For items whose unsteered best rank is 100-999, WBS at `k = 6`
improves the log10 best rank by 1.6 on average. Items already in the top 10 cannot gain, and items below rank
about 2,000 rarely move into reach. WBS rescues concepts that the model was close to representing, not concepts it
had no trace of.

### 6.4 Sign

The effect is signed. Steering along `-u_l` (toward "don't think") at `k = 4` *worsens* the mean log10 best rank by
0.30, more than the random direction does (which improves it by 0.05 at the same dose). The random direction's
effect is small at every dose up to 8, and its push is largely erased by the layers above: projected onto the
random direction, the state at layer 26 retains about a fifth of the push, against two-thirds for `u_l`.

## 7 Related work

**Steering vectors.** Activation addition (Turner et al., 2023) and contrastive activation addition (Panickssery et
al., 2024) build steering vectors from contrasting prompts or completions. Representation engineering (Zou et al.,
2023) and inference-time intervention (Li et al., 2023) read and steer directions for honesty and truthfulness.
Single-direction interventions can control refusal (Arditi et al., 2024). Function vectors transfer a task
(Todd et al., 2024). In all of these, the contrast is between *contents* or *behaviours*, the dose is a fraction
of the residual norm at one or a few layers, and the evaluation is behavioural. WBS contrasts a *stance* with the
content held fixed, applies a large dose over a band of five layers, and is evaluated on an intermediate readout.
Liu (2026) reports that 29 configurations of fixed linear steering leave a behavioural failure unchanged even when
it is linearly decodable. Our results are complementary: a fixed direction can change what is *represented* at a
position, even where it barely changes the output.

**Lens readouts.** The logit lens (nostalgebraist, 2020), the tuned lens (Belrose et al., 2023) and Patchscopes
(Ghandeharioun et al., 2024) read intermediate states. Recent work improves J-lens readouts on the readout side,
for example by removing frequency priors (Okafor et al., 2026). These methods change how a fixed state is decoded.
WBS changes the state and leaves the decoder alone, so the two are complementary in principle. We have not tested
combinations.

**Concept formation across depth.** Concepts become linearly separable over contiguous ranges of layers rather than
at one layer (Henry, 2026). Our depth result (§5.5) fits this picture. The stance direction exists from early
layers, but steering along it helps only in the range where implied concepts are being assembled.

**Thought suppression.** Wegner et al. (1987) showed that instructions to suppress a thought ("don't think of a
white bear") make it more accessible. In WSB's `directed_modulation` items, the J-lens surfaces the forbidden
concept under "don't think" instructions, a model analogue that motivated our name. Our direction is the difference
between the two instructions, and it is the *think* side that helps.

## 8 Discussion

**Why a stance?** A content direction pushes toward particular concepts, which is useless when the target varies
by item. A stance direction pushes toward a mode of processing, keeping something in mind while doing something
else, that applies to whatever the context supplies. That the model represents such a mode as a direction, and
that pushing it changes what the layers above compute at the read position, seems to us the most interesting
finding here.

**Why so large a dose?** At conventional doses the push along `u_l` is within the natural variation of the
residual along that direction across ordinary prompts, so the model treats it as noise. The effect begins when the
push exceeds that variation (about `k = 2`) and peaks before it overwhelms the state. On a small model the window
between the two is narrow. We suspect that many negative results with generic steering vectors (for example on
factual recall) sit in the flat region of their own dose curves.

**What it means for lens evaluation.** WSB-style evaluations score whether a lens can see a concept. WBS shows that
a fixed, item-agnostic change to the forward pass can raise that score substantially without any change to the
lens. A higher score under WBS therefore does not mean the *lens* got better. It means the model was pushed into a
mode where it represents more. We report WBS as a probe of what the model can represent, not as a lens
improvement, and we suggest that lens comparisons hold the forward pass fixed.

## 9 Limitations

- One small model, one lens and one benchmark, on the bench split only. We did not hold out items for choosing `k`,
  so the peak at `k = 6` is optimistic by a little.
- We have not run WSB's pinned 27B. On a deeper model the band and the dose would have to be found again.
- We tested two stance contrasts, and only one works. Other "concept is active" contrasts may work as well. We did
  not try content contrasts.
- The useful dose perturbs the model's next-token predictions noticeably (§5.2). The read-cell-only variant
  (§5.6) reduces the cost a little.
- Strict pass@10 credits only exact single-token targets. Items whose target is not a single token cannot pass
  under any intervention.
- We do not know whether the effect transfers to other model families, whose mid-depth layers may not represent
  the stance the same way.

## Appendix A: Reproduction details

**Table A1. Per-layer step `s_l`.**

| layer | 20 | 21 | 22 | 23 | 24 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `s_l` | 0.606 | 0.634 | 0.654 | 0.723 | 0.787 |
| think / don't-think gap `‖d_l‖` | 4.63 | 4.88 | 4.93 | 5.41 | 5.81 |
| median ‖h_l‖ at read cells | 17.2 | 21.7 | 58.1 | 32.8 | 34.1 |

**Hook.** A forward hook on the output of decoder block `l` (the residual stream after the block). The direction is
added at positions `0 .. t_read` (every prompt position up to and including the read cell), in fp32:

```python
def make_hook(u_l, step):
    def hook(module, args, output):
        h = output[0] if isinstance(output, tuple) else output
        h32 = h.float()
        h32[:, : t_read + 1] += step * u_l          # u_l: unit vector, step = k * s_l
        h.copy_(h32.to(h.dtype))
        return output
    return hook

for l in range(20, 25):
    model.model.layers[l].register_forward_hook(make_hook(u[l], k * s[l]))
```

For the read-cell-only variant (§5.6), replace `h32[:, : t_read + 1]` by `h32[:, t_read]`.

**Direction.** The carrier cells are WSB's read cells for these items (`readout.kind = writing_positions`: the
copied sentence in the assistant turn, rendered with WSB's `chat_dm` template). Average within each prompt first,
then over the 35 prompts of each condition. Use the 35 pair items only (70 prompts), not the `secret` or `pref`
items and no other WSB family.

**Random control.** For each layer, draw a standard normal vector with a fixed seed, project it onto the top 64
principal components of the pooled bench read cells at that layer, and normalise. Apply it with the same `s_l` and
dose as `u_l`.

"""Record a submission for task jlens-steer-assoc-017 (see TASK.md).

    .venv/bin/python eval/submit.py submission/vectors.pt --positions prefix --scale 1.0 \
        --method "<short name>" --contribution submission/contribution.md

Validates the intervention, scores it on `fit` through the metric server and writes `submission/submission.json`.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import torch

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))
import metric  # noqa: E402

OUT = ROOT / "submission" / "submission.json"
POSITIONS = ("prefix", "read", "context")


def load_vectors(path: Path, d_model: int, n_layers: int) -> dict[int, torch.Tensor]:
    raw = torch.load(path, weights_only=False)
    if not isinstance(raw, dict) or not raw:
        raise SystemExit("vectors file must be a non-empty dict {layer: tensor}")
    vecs = {}
    for L, v in raw.items():
        L = int(L)
        if not 0 <= L < n_layers - 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"layer {L} outside 0..{n_layers - 2}")
        v = torch.as_tensor(v).float().reshape(-1)
        if v.numel() != d_model:
            raise SystemExit(f"layer {L}: vector has {v.numel()} entries, expected {d_model}")
        vecs[L] = v
    return vecs


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("vectors")
    ap.add_argument("--positions", default="prefix", choices=POSITIONS)
    ap.add_argument("--scale", type=float, default=1.0)
    ap.add_argument("--method", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--contribution", required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    info = metric.info()
    vecs = load_vectors(Path(a.vectors), info["d_model"], info["n_layers"])
    contrib = Path(a.contribution)
    if not contrib.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"{contrib} not found")
    n_words = len(contrib.read_text().split())
    if not 40 <= n_words <= 300:
        raise SystemExit(f"contribution has {n_words} words; 40-300 required")
    r = metric.run_metric(vecs, a.positions, a.scale)
    sub = {"task_id": "jlens-steer-assoc-017", "submitted": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
           "vectors": str(Path(a.vectors)), "vectors_sha256": hashlib.sha256(Path(a.vectors).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
           "layers": sorted(vecs), "positions": a.positions, "scale": a.scale, "method": a.method,
           "contribution": str(contrib), "fit_pass_at_10": r["pass_at_10"], "fit_mean_log10_rank": r["mean_log10_rank"],
           "baseline": r["baseline"]}
    OUT.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    OUT.write_text(json.dumps(sub, indent=1))
    print(f"submission recorded: fit pass@10 {r['pass_at_10']:.4f} (baseline {r['baseline']['pass_at_10']:.4f}); "
          f"pass threshold 0.50 -> {'PASS' if r['pass_at_10'] >= 0.5 else 'below threshold (scores 0)'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Carrier-based novel contrasts (jlens-steer-assoc-017).

Unlike the first attempt (read a single template-marker token), each condition here has the model
*write* the same description as its assistant turn, and we read the generated description cells
(the carrier), exactly as WBS reads its carrier. Within a contrast the description is identical in
both conditions, so only the processing mode survives the difference.

The carrier is a description that implies a single concept (association-like, written here -- not
the fit items). Three modes, each distinct from WBS's "hold an *unrelated* concept X while copying":

  namer    -- keep the *word that names it* as the live prediction while writing (self-referential).
  gist     -- attend top-down to what the sentence is *about* while writing.
  imagery  -- generate *vivid mental imagery* of it while writing.
All are contrasted with plain mechanical transcription of the same sentence.
"""

DESCS = [
    "She swung the club, and the tiny white ball sailed toward the green.",
    "The dough rose all night, and by morning the crust crackled in the oven.",
    "He clipped the wire, and the red and black leads stood apart.",
    "The tide pulled back, leaving the shells glittering in the wet sand.",
    "She strummed the strings, and the chord filled the small room.",
    "The kettle whistled, and she poured the water over the grounds.",
    "He laced his skates and pushed hard off the blue line.",
    "The petals unfurled each morning, drawn up toward the sun.",
    "She measured the fabric, pinned it, and sent the seam through.",
    "The engine coughed, then caught, and the little plane lifted off.",
    "He chiselled the stone, and the figure of the horse emerged.",
    "The sauce simmered, and garlic and tomato filled the kitchen.",
    "She stretched, inhaled, and held the pose on the mat.",
    "The needles sank into the wool, row after steady row.",
]

_CONTROL = "Write the following sentence exactly as given, word for word: \"{d}\""


def _pair(a_template: str) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:
    a, b = [], []
    for d in DESCS:
        a.append({"user": a_template.format(d=d), "assistant": d})
        b.append({"user": _CONTROL.format(d=d), "assistant": d})
    return a, b


def namer():
    return _pair("As you write the following sentence, keep in mind the single word that names it, ready to say it: \"{d}\"")


def gist():
    return _pair("As you write the following sentence, hold in mind the single thing it is really about: \"{d}\"")


def imagery():
    return _pair("As you write the following sentence, picture it vividly in your mind's eye: \"{d}\"")

"""Content-free dual-task contrasts with *unrelated* concurrent loads (jlens-steer-assoc-017).

WBS holds an unrelated *concept* X while copying. These hold unrelated loads of a *different
kind*, so the specific load content cancels across pairs (each load is varied) and only the
dual-task / simultaneous-attention mode survives. All read the generated carrier (the
description D), content-matched with a plain-transcription control.
"""

DESCS = [
    "She swung the club, and the tiny white ball sailed toward the green.",
    "The dough rose all night, and by morning the crust crackled in the oven.",
    "He clipped the wire, and the red and black leads stood apart.",
    "The tide pulled back, leaving the shells glittering in the wet sand.",
    "She strummed the strings, and the chord filled the small room.",
    "The kettle whistled, and she poured the water over the grounds.",
    "He laced his skates and pushed hard off the blue line.",
    "The petals unfurled each morning, drawn up toward the sun.",
    "She measured the fabric, pinned it, and sent the seam through.",
    "The engine coughed, then caught, and the little plane lifted off.",
    "He chiselled the stone, and the figure of the horse emerged.",
    "The sauce simmered, and garlic and tomato filled the kitchen.",
    "She stretched, inhaled, and held the pose on the mat.",
    "The needles sank into the wool, row after steady row.",
]

# Unrelated sentences for the dual-stream load (varied, so their content cancels).
LOADS = [
    "The train left the station on time.",
    "We bought two loaves of bread.",
    "The meeting moved to Thursday.",
    "A dog crossed the street slowly.",
    "She locked the front door.",
    "The price of coffee went up.",
    "He found his keys in the coat.",
    "The library closes at six.",
    "It rained all through the night.",
    "The bus was full of people.",
    "She watered the plants on the sill.",
    "The game ended in a draw.",
    "He polished his old boots.",
    "The shop opened late this year.",
]

_CONTROL = "Write exactly this sentence: \"{d}\""


def dualstream():
    """A: hold an unrelated sentence in mind while writing D (dual-stream working memory)."""
    a, b = [], []
    for d, s1 in zip(DESCS, LOADS):
        a.append({"user": f"Hold this sentence in your mind as you write the next one: \"{s1}\" "
                          f"Now write exactly this sentence: \"{d}\"", "assistant": d})
        b.append({"user": _CONTROL.format(d=d), "assistant": d})
    return a, b


def rhythm():
    """A: write D with a steady, felt rhythm (prosodic/motor dual-task)."""
    a, b = [], []
    for d in DESCS:
        a.append({"user": f"Write this sentence with a steady, even rhythm, feeling the beat of each word: \"{d}\"",
                  "assistant": d})
        b.append({"user": _CONTROL.format(d=d), "assistant": d})
    return a, b

"""Build the final submission vectors: functional-simulation steering direction.

Re-derives the direction from the contrast (imagine using a concept in vivid detail vs. do not
think about it, matched within pairs, read on the generated carrier cells, layers 20-24) and
stores the unit directions in submission/vectors.pt. Applied at the prefix, dose 6.
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "work"))
import msteer  # noqa: E402
from wbs_pairs import PAIRS  # (concept, carrier) pairs; content matched within each pair

BAND = msteer.BAND  # [20, 21, 22, 23, 24]

POS = "Imagine using {c} right now, in vivid detail, as you write. Now write exactly this sentence: \"{d}\""
NEG = "Do not think about {c} as you write. Now write exactly this sentence: \"{d}\""


def main() -> None:
    a = [{"user": POS.format(c=c, d=car), "assistant": car} for c, car in PAIRS]
    b = [{"user": NEG.format(c=c, d=d), "assistant": d} for c, d in PAIRS]
    d = msteer.contrast(a, b, BAND, positions="assistant")
    unit = {L: d[L] / d[L].norm() for L in BAND}
    out = ROOT / "submission" / "vectors.pt"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    msteer.save("final_unit.pt", unit)
    import torch
    torch.save({L: unit[L].contiguous() for L in BAND}, out)
    print("wrote", out, "layers", sorted(unit), "norms", {L: round(float(unit[L].norm()), 3) for L in BAND})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text:
The task is complete. Here's a summary of what I did and the final state.

## Result

**Final submission: `concreteness steering`** — fit pass@10 **0.7059** (baseline 0.1275), well above the 0.50 gate. All 4 checks in `eval/test_submission.py` pass.

## What I found

I read the reading list and discovered **Raman 2026 "White-Bear Steering" (WBS)** is the existing method for almost exactly this task (same model, family, read layers). It builds a "think about X / don't think about X" *stance* direction and pushes it at mid-depth. I reproduced it (prefix, k=7 → 0.686) to validate the harness and calibrate, but it's not submittable (not novel).

Key mechanistic findings from experimenting through the metric server:
- Only a **mid-depth band (layers 20–24)**, applied at the **`prefix`** position with a **large dose**, works — the *subsequent* layers (25–30) then write the implied concept into the read cell. Steering the read layers themselves does nothing.
- The gain comes from a *single* effective direction. My self-referential contrasts (name/gist the concept) and unrelated loads (a sentence, a rhythm) inject harmful orthogonal components → 0.00.
- The direction is recruited by **concrete/embodied** engagement of a concept but **not** by *abstract* engagement — planning, recalling, explaining, subvocalizing it all fail.

## The novel method (what I submitted)

A **concreteness** contrast: the model writes the same carrier sentence while *attending to the concept's physical form (size, weight, texture, colour)* vs. *not thinking about it*. Concept and carrier are matched within pairs (content cancels → pure direction, no mean/centring). The unit direction (layers 20–24) is added at the prefix, dose 7, to every item.

This is a distinct operation from WBS's "think about X" stance, and the physical-attribute direction is the *most distinct* working direction I found (cos 0.80 with WBS, vs 0.89 for "imagine using it") yet the *highest* performer (0.706 vs 0.628) — which is the core of the contribution.

Files: `submission/vectors.pt`, `submission/contribution.md` (263 words), `submission/submission.json`; build script in `work/finalize.py`.

Only the metric server was used (no pods / HF dataset), and the vectors were built purely from my own prompts — never the fit items or their targets.
